title: Thread-Safe LRU Cache
summary: Build a fixed-capacity, thread-safe in-memory cache with O(1) operations, LRU and FIFO eviction chosen at creation, optional per-entry expiry and hit/miss statistics.
statement:
Several services in your company each hand-roll a small in-memory cache in front of slow lookups such as prices and user profiles. You are building one reusable cache library they can all share.

**Behaviour**
- A cache is created with a capacity — the maximum number of entries it may hold, at least 1 — and an eviction policy.
- Callers can get a value by key, put a key–value pair, remove a key, and ask for the current number of entries. Null keys and null values are rejected.
- Putting a key that is already present replaces its value and never evicts anything.
- When a put adds a new key to a full cache, exactly one existing entry is evicted first, chosen by the eviction policy.
- Two eviction policies are required, chosen when the cache is created:
  - **Least recently used (LRU)** — evict the entry whose last get or put is the oldest.
  - **First in, first out (FIFO)** — evict the entry that was inserted earliest; reads and value updates do not change its position.
- Further policies, such as least frequently used, are expected later; teams want to add them without touching the rest of the cache.

**Expiry (optional, per entry)**
A put may give a time-to-live. Once the current time reaches the insertion time plus the time-to-live, the entry is never returned again: a get treats it as missing and removes it. Expired entries may occupy space until they are read or evicted. Updating a key gives it the new put's time-to-live (none if omitted).

**Statistics**
The cache counts hits, misses and evictions since it was created.

**Performance and concurrency**
- get, put and remove must take O(1) average time regardless of capacity, which can be up to one million entries.
- One cache instance is shared by many request-handling threads. Every operation must behave as if it happened atomically at a single instant, and the cache must stay correct however the threads interleave.

requirements.text: Create a cache with a capacity of at least 1 and an eviction policy (LRU or FIFO); an invalid capacity or missing policy is rejected.

Getting a key returns its value if the entry is present and not expired, otherwise reports it missing. Under LRU a successful get makes the entry the most recently used; under FIFO it changes nothing.

Putting a key and value inserts a new entry or replaces the value of an existing one. Replacing never evicts and does not change the number of entries; under LRU it makes the entry most recently used, under FIFO it keeps its original position.
When a put adds a new key to a full cache, evict exactly one entry first — the least recently used under LRU, the earliest inserted under FIFO — so the number of entries never exceeds the capacity.
Removing a key deletes its entry and reports whether it was present; the size reported is the number of entries currently held, including expired entries not yet removed.
All operations are safe to call concurrently from many threads on one cache instance, with the guarantees given in the concurrency notes.

Support an optional positive time-to-live per put: an entry is expired once now ≥ insertion time + TTL, is never returned after that, and is removed when a get finds it expired. A zero or negative TTL is rejected.
Report statistics: hits (gets that returned a value), misses (gets that did not, including expired entries) and evictions (entries removed to make room).

constraints: Java 17 or later using only the standard library (java.util.concurrent is allowed); JUnit 5 may be used for tests.
Do not rely on a library collection that already implements access ordering or eviction (for example LinkedHashMap in access-order mode or its eldest-entry removal hook) or on caching libraries.
get, put and remove must run in O(1) average time; capacity can be up to 1,000,000 entries.
Single JVM process with all state in memory.
Expiry time comes from a clock that tests can control; millisecond precision.
assumptions: Keys have correct equals and hashCode implementations and are not mutated while in the cache.
Values are treated as opaque; no defensive copies are needed.
Capacity is fixed for the life of a cache.

examples.title: LRU order
examples.scenario: LRU cache, capacity 3: put a=1, b=2, c=3; get a; put d=4; get b; put c=30; put e=5.
examples.expected: get a returns 1. Putting d evicts b (least recently used). get b is a miss. put c=30 replaces c without eviction. Putting e evicts a. Final contents d=4, c=30, e=5; size 3; hits 1, misses 1, evictions 2.

examples.title: FIFO ignores reads and updates
examples.scenario: FIFO cache, capacity 2: put x=1, y=2; get x; put z=3; put y=20; put w=4.
examples.expected: Putting z evicts x (inserted first, even though it was just read). put y=20 replaces y in place and keeps its original position. Putting w evicts y. Final contents z=3, w=4.

examples.title: Expiry boundary
examples.scenario: LRU cache, capacity 2. At t=0 ms put k=v with a TTL of 10,000 ms. get k at t=9,999 ms; get k at t=10,000 ms.
examples.expected: The first get returns v (hit). The second is a miss because the entry has expired; k is removed and size becomes 0.

examples.title: Contention
examples.scenario: LRU cache, capacity 100. 8 threads start together; each puts 10,000 distinct keys of its own (80,000 distinct keys overall) interleaved with 10,000 gets of random keys from the whole key range.
examples.expected: No exceptions. Afterwards size is exactly 100, hits + misses = 80,000, evictions = 79,900 (80,000 inserts − 100 remaining), and every value returned by a get was the value put for that key.

edgeCases: Capacity 1: every new key evicts the previous entry.
A put of an existing key into a full cache evicts nothing.
A get of a missing key does not change the recency of other entries.
remove of a missing key returns false and does not change the statistics.
Null key or null value is rejected and the cache is unchanged.
A zero or negative TTL is rejected; updating a key with no TTL makes it never expire.
The cache is full of expired-but-unread entries: a new put still evicts according to the policy.
outOfScope: Sharing a cache across processes or machines.
Persisting or spilling entries to disk.
Loading missing values automatically on a miss.
Capacity measured in bytes rather than entries.

concurrency.notes: Must be thread-safe: get, put, remove, size and statistics may be called concurrently on one cache from many threads. Guarantees: (1) every operation is atomic — it behaves as if it ran alone at some instant between its call and return; (2) once any operation returns, the number of entries does not exceed capacity; (3) no lost updates: concurrent puts of distinct keys that fit within capacity are all present afterwards; (4) a get only returns a value that was put for that key; (5) statistics are exact — hits + misses equals completed gets and evictions equals entries evicted; (6) internal ordering is never corrupted: no exceptions, lost or duplicated entries under contention. Correctness under contention is required; throughput is secondary.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The LRU and FIFO examples produce exactly the stated evictions, final contents and statistics.
Updating an existing key in a full cache never evicts, under both policies.
remove reports presence correctly and size reflects inserts, updates, removals and evictions.
With a controlled clock an entry is returned 1 ms before its expiry and missing at the expiry instant, and is then removed.
The contention example passes repeatedly: size exactly 100, hits + misses = 80,000, evictions = 79,900, no exceptions.
Null keys/values, capacity below 1 and non-positive TTLs are rejected without changing the cache.

stretchGoals.text: Add a least-frequently-used policy, breaking ties by least recently used, without changing the get/put code paths.
Let callers be told about every entry that leaves the cache, with its key, value and the reason (evicted, expired or removed).

rubricGuidance.correctness: FR-2 to FR-5 carry the weight: check exact recency and insertion-order behaviour from the worked examples (updates without eviction, FIFO ignoring reads) and that eviction happens only when a new key is added to a full cache.
rubricGuidance.modeling: Expect the bookkeeping that chooses an eviction victim to be separable from key-to-value storage, so LRU and FIFO differ only in that bookkeeping. Expiry and statistics should not be entangled with policy-specific code.
rubricGuidance.principles: Internal ordering structures must never be exposed to callers, and invariants (size ≤ capacity, storage and ordering agree) should be maintained in one place. Concurrency is required: check-then-act gaps between lookup, eviction and insertion are serious defects, whatever mechanism is used.
rubricGuidance.extensibility: The statement explicitly anticipates new eviction policies (e.g. LFU); adding one should not require changing get/put logic. That one seam is justified — further speculative abstraction (swappable storage, generic event systems) should not earn credit.
rubricGuidance.readability: Any custom ordering bookkeeping should be small, well named and easy to verify; coordination code should be visibly separate from data-structure logic.
rubricGuidance.edge_cases: Check capacity 1, updates in a full cache, null keys and values, the TTL boundary (expired exactly at insertion + TTL), invalid TTL and capacity, and removal of absent keys.
rubricGuidance.tests: Expect deterministic tests for LRU and FIFO order and for expiry with a controlled clock, plus at least one multi-threaded test asserting size and exact statistics after contention.
